Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. submission.text: will have one RD wide BAA to monitor on SAM.gov instead of multiple BAAs across the Directorate • Why do we need another contracting tool separate from DETER? • Selecting the right contracting tool for the job leads to the best outcomes. TACTICAL BAA fills a gap for pursuing FAR-based awards for 6.1-6.4 efforts that was not available previously at the directorate level. TACTICAL will complement other tools such as the DETER ARA, SBIR/STTRs, and grants & cooperative agreements under the upcoming RAD Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA). • What if a technically qualified offeror wants to join a Topic Area Group, but missed the normal deadline? • The offeror can either wait and submit during the next annual period (every January) or AFRL can choose to release an interim request for additional executive summaries. • Will these slides be available online or via email? •The slide will be emailed to all registered participants, along with the Q&A, and will also be posted to the sam.gov DETER Virtual Industry Day announcement. • When will the next closed call be released? •Please keep monitoring the TACTICAL SAM.gov posting and sign up for notification of changes. This will notify you when there are changes or a Call announcement is made under TACTICAL. AFRL-2023-4752 Approved

Introduction Purpose: The purpose of this project is to update the Hatchery building’s air-conditioning system. Background: The Hatchery Building was originally constructed in 1962 and consists of unreinforced concrete blocks on concrete stem walls and slab on grade. Exterior and load bearing walls were constructed with 8” blocks with pilasters constructed of 12” block. Non-load bearing walls and short walls utilize 4” and 6” blocks. The roof system consists of open web joists bearing on either masonry walls or wider flanged beams with 5/8” plywood deck and a flat roof. sla_onsite.text: Printing's (BEP) Facility located in Washington, DC contains an Industrial Wastewater Pretreatment Plant (WWPP). BEP's objective is to procure contractor services to manage, operate, maintain supplies and perform maintenance and provide technical support for the Wastewater and Storm Water Programs. The WWPP requires services to support the BEP on a 24/7 basis. The WWPP currently consists of four (4) systems: (1) Wiping Solution Wastewater Pretreatment Plant (WSWPP), (2) Plating Wastewater Pretreatment Plant (PWPP), (3) Grease Trap Wastewater Pretreatment Plant (GTWPP), and (4) Wiping Solution Recycling Plant (WSRP). The WWPP includes an on-site lab and a materials storage area. Refer to Attachments 2, 3, 4, and 5 for descriptions of the four (4) systems as well as Attachment 9 and 10 for listings of the equipment that are part of the WSWPP and PWPP, respectively. The GTWPP may be removed during the course of this contract. In addition to these systems, additional systems are currently being researched that will be included in the scope of this requirement. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. submission.text: will have one RD wide BAA to monitor on SAM.gov instead of multiple BAAs across the Directorate • Why do we need another contracting tool separate from DETER? • Selecting the right contracting tool for the job leads to the best outcomes. TACTICAL BAA fills a gap for pursuing FAR-based awards for 6.1-6.4 efforts that was not available previously at the directorate level. TACTICAL will complement other tools such as the DETER ARA, SBIR/STTRs, and grants & cooperative agreements under the upcoming RAD Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA). • What if a technically qualified offeror wants to join a Topic Area Group, but missed the normal deadline? • The offeror can either wait and submit during the next annual period (every January) or AFRL can choose to release an interim request for additional executive summaries. • Will these slides be available online or via email? •The slide will be emailed to all registered participants, along with the Q&A, and will also be posted to the sam.gov DETER Virtual Industry Day announcement. • When will the next closed call be released? •Please keep monitoring the TACTICAL SAM.gov posting and sign up for notification of changes. This will notify you when there are changes or a Call announcement is made under TACTICAL. AFRL-2023-4752 Approved

Introduction Purpose: The purpose of this project is to update the Hatchery building’s air-conditioning system. Background: The Hatchery Building was originally constructed in 1962 and consists of unreinforced concrete blocks on concrete stem walls and slab on grade. Exterior and load bearing walls were constructed with 8” blocks with pilasters constructed of 12” block. Non-load bearing walls and short walls utilize 4” and 6” blocks. The roof system consists of open web joists bearing on either masonry walls or wider flanged beams with 5/8” plywood deck and a flat roof. sla_onsite.text: Printing's (BEP) Facility located in Washington, DC contains an Industrial Wastewater Pretreatment Plant (WWPP). BEP's objective is to procure contractor services to manage, operate, maintain supplies and perform maintenance and provide technical support for the Wastewater and Storm Water Programs. The WWPP requires services to support the BEP on a 24/7 basis. The WWPP currently consists of four (4) systems: (1) Wiping Solution Wastewater Pretreatment Plant (WSWPP), (2) Plating Wastewater Pretreatment Plant (PWPP), (3) Grease Trap Wastewater Pretreatment Plant (GTWPP), and (4) Wiping Solution Recycling Plant (WSRP). The WWPP includes an on-site lab and a materials storage area. Refer to Attachments 2, 3, 4, and 5 for descriptions of the four (4) systems as well as Attachment 9 and 10 for listings of the equipment that are part of the WSWPP and PWPP, respectively. The GTWPP may be removed during the course of this contract. In addition to these systems, additional systems are currently being researched that will be included in the scope of this requirement.
